glossary.definition:
The portion of a cell cycle when no replication is in progress.
B = τ − C − D. Under succinate (τ ≈ 82, C = 40, D = 20), B ≈ 22 min.
Required > 0 for a non-overlapping cell cycle with single-shot
replication initiation per generation.

Replication elongation time — chromosome-completion duration from
initiation. ParCa-default for succinate: 40 min.

Post-replication-termination delay before division. ParCa-default:
20 min. Enforced by MarkDPeriod + Division step (see Round 3.7
D-period wiring fix on feat/dnaa-mock-investigation-start, commit
8b5d8cd) — pull forward before running dnaa-0.

Runtime overwrite of dnaA's per-promoter init_prob via
sim_data.genetic_perturbations["TU00259[c]"] = 2e-3. PDF feedback's
working solution for dnaa-1; leaves baseline dnaA TE (0.35), mRNA
t½ (1.9 min), and protein t½ (280 min) unchanged.

Replication origin on the E. coli chromosome. Count goes 1 → 2 when
replication initiates, returns to 1 at division when chromosomes
segregate to daughters. AT STEADY STATE under succinate (gen 3
onwards), oriC oscillates 1 ↔ 2; reaching 4 there would mean
re-initiation before division (overlapping cycles). NOTE: during the
pre-steady-state transient (gens 1–2) a brief overshoot to 4 is
expected and is the signature that the lineage has not yet settled
onto the periodic attractor (Rashmi 2026-05-30) — it is not a
failure of the succinate regime.

Per-cell observables (oriC, cell_mass, DnaA count) are periodic in
the followed-daughter lineage — same value at the same phase of
every cycle. Reached after a few generations of transient decay
from the initial condition.

The transcription unit identifier for the dnaA operon
(dnaA-dnaN-recF) on the chromosome. Mechanism A targets this TU's
per-promoter init_prob to tune dnaA mRNA synthesis rate.

biological_story:
In a real E. coli cell, the decision to start a new round of chromosome
replication is made by the protein DnaA, gated by oriC site occupancy.
Under fast growth (τ short relative to C+D), replication initiates
multiple times before division and the cell can have 4+ oriC. Under
slower growth (τ > C+D, the regime this investigation targets), each
cell cycle has a free B-period where the cell isn't replicating; the
cycle proceeds 1 oriC → initiation → 2 oriC → C-period replication →
D-period delay → division → 1 oriC.

This investigation pulls v2ecoli into the slower regime via succinate
(ParCa fit: τ ≈ 82 min, C = 40 min, D = 20 min, B = 22 min) and asks
two foundational questions before any mechanism is built on top:
(1) does v2ecoli actually settle into the periodic regime succinate
predicts, and (2) once it does, can the DnaA pool be held in the
physiological literature band stably across generations?

Step 1 — succinate steady state. Run for 10 generations with
single_daughters tracking, check per-cell oriC and cell_mass are
periodic in the followed daughter lineage. After ~3 generations the
transient should decay; from generation 3 onwards, the lineage looks
like the PDF's exemplar trace: cell mass sawtooths 600 → 1200 → 600
fg per cycle, oriC steps 1 → 2 → 1 once per cycle. Save the gen-N
state as the canonical succinate initial condition for subsequent
studies.

Step 2 — DnaA expression tuning. With the canonical initial condition
in hand, apply Mechanism A (runtime overwrite of TU00259[c]'s
per-promoter init_prob to 2e-3) and check the DnaA monomer count
(sum across forms) lands in [300, 800] and stays stable across the
7+ generation lineage.
question:
Can v2ecoli reproduce DnaA-driven replication initiation in succinate at
STEADY STATE — periodic oriC + cell-mass + DnaA dynamics across multiple
generations — using ParCa's native succinate parameters with no imposed
τ / C / D overrides?
hypothesis:
In succinate (τ ≈ 70–80 min, ParCa-default C = 40 min, D = 20 min,
B = τ − C − D > 0), v2ecoli with a tuned dnaA RNA-synthesis probability
(Mechanism A: sim_data.genetic_perturbations["TU00259[c]"] = 2e-3
runtime overwrite) holds the DnaA monomer pool in the literature
[300, 800] band across generations and produces a non-overlapping cell
cycle that initiates replication exactly once per cycle. The cycle
proceeds: cell starts with 1 oriC, replication initiates once near the
end of B-period, oriC briefly doubles to 2, replication completes after
C-period, D-period elapses, division fires, daughters start the same
cycle again — never reaching 4 oriC simultaneously.

The earlier ~0.997 DnaA-ATP pin was diagnosed (Haochen) as a FAST-EQUILIBRIUM
artefact, not a parameter error: v2ecoli integrated the DnaA-ADP binding to
steady state each tick, instantly reverting hydrolysis-made DnaA-ADP. Haochen's
bf8b82e mechanism (commit ADOPTED) keeps the DnaA-ADP reaction bidirectional but
flags it integrate_dt=true (kinetic, literal k_r=1×10⁻⁷/s) and adds DnaA-ATP
intrinsic hydrolysis (k=0.046/min) as a one-way kinetic reaction. This drives
the DnaA-ATP fraction OFF the pin and INTO the Boesen [0.2,0.5] band.

dnaa-3 (2026-06-07/08): the in-sim DnaA-box binding fires correctly inside the simulation as the PROVIDED read-only occupancy listener (4 affinity pools, fast equilibrium, full box set; three wiring fixes: bulk port type, read-only output topology, emitter overwrite-vs-accumulate). It reports free DnaA-ATP and per-pool occupancy with the dnaa-2 cell cycle preserved exactly. CORRECTION (Rashmi 2026-06-08): an earlier pass had added a box-capacity cap=32 justified by outside ChIP-seq (Smith 2024) plus a DnaA sink and abundance/datA literature — none of which were provided. These have been WITHDRAWN; only the provided mechanisms are modeled. The DnaA-ATP fraction is in band (0.23), but free DnaA-ATP stays ~380-550 nM — ≈4× the 100 nM oriC-low K_d — for 100% of every cycle across all 7 generations, so oriC-low occupancy holds ~0.8 throughout (high-affinity pools saturate). The withdrawn ideas (Smith ChIP-seq, abundance, datA) are recorded as proposed_inputs for Rashmi to Accept or Decline in the report.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
Under ParCa-default succinate, v2ecoli reaches a non-overlapping
periodic cell cycle (oriC 1↔2 at steady state, from gen 3 onwards —
a transient overshoot to 4 in the first generations marks the
pre-steady-state relaxation) AND, with the 2e-3 dnaA init_prob
runtime overwrite, the dnaA mRNA initiation rate lands near the
biologically-expected ≈1 event/min, which in turn holds the DnaA
monomer pool in the Schmidt 2016 / Mori 2021 [300, 800] band stably
across generations.

The dnaA init rate at V=0.8e-3 is ~0.6/min (gens 4-7 0.65/0.46/0.57/0.71) — sub-physiological vs the ~1/min target: the KNOWN TRADEOFF (init-rate test PARTIAL). No single CONSTITUTIVE V closes both the in-band pool AND the ~1/min rate (7-point sweep + the 15-gen V=1.1e-3 equilibration run that overshoots the band then relaxes) — closing both needs a regulated / cell-cycle-coupled DnaA synthesis lever (for Rashmi/Haochen). The earlier V=1.1e-3 pick is WITHDRAWN (its 7-gen "676 in-band" reading was a pre-equilibration artifact). Steady-state dynamics are seed-robust (multiseed seeds 0-3). Pending Rashmi's confirmation. evidence_against: Within each cycle the DnaA pool OSCILLATES above the [300,800] band at its pre-division peak (≈1000) before halving at division — so the band holds for the cycle-MEAN, not every instantaneous tick. studies.name: dnaa-0-succinate-baseline
studies.title: Study 0 — Establish Succinate Steady State
studies.question:
Does v2ecoli, under the ParCa-default succinate growth condition with no
imposed τ / C / D overrides, reach a per-cell periodic steady state in
a single_daughters lineage — oriC count oscillating 1 ↔ 2 at steady
state (gen 3 onwards), with cell mass periodic in phase? A transient
overshoot to 4 in the first generations is allowed and expected (it
marks the pre-steady-state relaxation; Rashmi 2026-05-30). If yes, save
the gen-3 state as the canonical succinate steady-state initial
condition for subsequent studies in this investigation.

resolved_uncertainties: Under ParCa-default succinate with no τ/C/D overrides, the single-daughters lineage reaches a periodic steady state by generation 3 (oriC 1↔2, cell-mass sawtooth CV ≤ 4.5%) — establishing a valid baseline cell cycle for the DnaA studies.
The gen-1–2 oriC overshoot to 4 is the expected pre-steady-state relaxation (reviewer-confirmed), not a defect; gen 3 is the correct burned-in state to save as the canonical initial condition.
The unregulated baseline DnaA monomer pool sits far below the literature [300,800] band (per-gen mean declining 44→4), quantifying the calibration gap dnaa-1 must close.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the gen-1–2 transient overshoot to 4 oriC is purely an initial-condition artefact or has any seed/parameter sensitivity — only seed 0 was run, and the 5-gen lineage was accepted in place of the spec's 10 generations.
How robust the periodic 1↔2 steady state is to seed variation, since the canonical run is a single seed.

alternate_hypotheses.statement: The gen-1–2 oriC overshoot to 4 (and the short gen-2 τ of 52 min) is an artefact of the resume-from-gen-1 daughter initial condition, not an intrinsic property of the succinate attractor.
alternate_hypotheses.why_plausible: The overshoot appears only in the first generations and disappears from gen 3 onward; gen 2 also has the shortest τ, both consistent with a state not yet aligned with the periodic attractor.
evidence_for: oriC visits {1,2,4} only in gens 1–2 then settles to {1,2}
gen-2 τ (52 min) is an outlier vs the gen 3–5 regime (73–80 min)
evidence_against: only a single seed was run, so an intrinsic-dynamics explanation cannot be excluded

mechanism_update_proposals.rationale: The periodic 1↔2 steady state with periodic cell mass validates the succinate baseline as the reference cell cycle for the downstream DnaA studies.

studies.name: dnaa-1-expression
studies.title: Study 1 — Tune DnaA Expression
studies.question:
Does Mechanism A — runtime overwrite of
sim_data.genetic_perturbations["TU00259[c]"] = 2e-3 — reproduce the PDF
feedback exemplar: DnaA monomer count (summed across all DnaA forms)
stably in the literature [300, 800] band across a 7+ generation
succinate lineage starting from dnaa-0's saved steady-state initial
condition? If V = 2e-3 doesn't reproduce, what value does?

resolved_uncertainties: Mechanism A (runtime overwrite of TU00259[c]'s per-promoter init_prob) is the right lever for dnaA expression — sweeping V down to 0.8e-3 holds the DnaA monomer cycle-mean band-stable in [300,800] for steady gens 4-7 (337/338/360/415, peaks <800) with a clean oriC 1↔2 cycle. The chosen V undershoots the ~1/min init-rate target (0.46–0.71/min); the rate hits target at V≈1.0e-3, where the pool ramps out of band — the two acceptance layers are in tension.
monomer_counts[3861] (PD03831[c], idx 3861) already aggregates all DnaA forms, so it is usable directly as the DnaA pool observable (Rashmi build-note resolved).
The in-band DnaA pool is the downstream CONSEQUENCE of hitting the initiation-rate target, not an independent knob (the acceptance is reframed as a rate check).

resolved_uncertainties.The init-rate vs band-stable-pool tensio: at the chosen V=0.8e-3 the DnaA pool is band-stable but the init rate (0.46–0.71/min) is sub-physiological; at V≈1.0e-3 the rate is on target but the pool ramps out of band by gen 7. No single V in this sweep satisfies BOTH layers at the dnaa-0 succinate initial condition — resolving this may need a different lever (e.g. cell-cycle-coupled synthesis or a different starting DnaA pool).

resolved_uncertainties: The lineage starts from dnaa-0's low (~12 monomer) baseline and RAMPS for several generations before settling; "steady state" is reached only by gen 4 even at the chosen V. Whether a longer lineage drifts further (the 0.8e-3 cycle-mean still creeps 337→415) is untested.
All sweep runs are single-seed (seed 1); cross-seed stability of the in-band pool is untested.

alternate_hypotheses.statement: The pre-division peak excursion above 800 is intrinsic to DnaA's once-per-cycle accumulate-and-halve dynamics and cannot be removed by V-tuning alone without pushing the trough below the band.
alternate_hypotheses.why_plausible: Lowering V proportionally lowers peak, trough, and init rate together; below ~1.6e-3 the trough drops under 300 and the lineage equilibrates more slowly (V=1.5e-3 CV 10.9%), so no single V holds the full oscillation in a 2.67×-wide band.
evidence_for: V=1.5e-3 trough 288 (<300), CV 10.9%; V=1.7e-3 cycle-mean in band but peak 854–934
the band spans only 2.67× while the pool doubles per cycle
evidence_against: degradation/regulation levers other than V (e.g. cell-cycle-coupled synthesis) were not explored

findings.summary:
The DnaA monomer pool is a per-cycle SAWTOOTH — it accumulates through
the cycle and roughly halves at division, so the pre-division PEAK is
≈2× the post-division TROUGH. The literature band [300, 800] spans only a
2.67× window, so the whole oscillation cannot sit inside it unless the
trough is held in [300, 400] and the peak in [600, 800] — a narrow target.
Lowering V reduces the peak but proportionally lowers the trough and the
init rate, and below ~1.6e-3 the trough dips under 300 and the lineage
equilibrates more slowly (V=1.5e-3: CV 10.9%, trough 288). The band is
therefore best read as the cycle-TYPICAL level (cycle-mean), which sits
mid-band at every tested V; the instantaneous peak excursion above 800 is
intrinsic to DnaA's once-per-cycle accumulate-and-halve dynamics.
findings.statement: Total DnaA abundance doubles once per division cycle (run dnaa1-mechA-1.7e-3-7gen), confirming that DnaA synthesis tracks the cell cycle and the protein pool is replenished each generation as expected.

findings.summary:
V-sweep (2026-06-08, Rashmi's request) over {1.7e-3, 1.0e-3, 0.8e-3} via the
recorded --perturbation override on one shared cache, full per-gen history,
seed 1, 7 gens. The DnaA monomer cycle-mean RAMPS up from dnaa-0's low
baseline and where it settles scales with V: at V=1.7e-3 it ramps OUT of
band (→1131 by gen 7), at V=1.0e-3 it ramps to the band edge (→832, gens 3-6
in band), and at V=0.8e-3 it PLATEAUS in band (gens 4-7: 337/338/360/415,
peaks <800). Lowering V both lowers the plateau AND slows the ramp, so
0.8e-3 is the lowest tested V that holds the whole per-cycle oscillation
inside [300,800] for the steady generations with a clean oriC 1↔2 cycle.
HONEST TRADEOFF: at 0.8e-3 the init rate (0.46–0.71/min) undershoots the
~1/min target; the rate is on target only at V≈1.0e-3, where the pool is not
band-stable. The two acceptance layers (band-stable pool vs ~1/min rate) are
in tension at the dnaa-0 succinate initial condition.
findings.statement: Sweeping the dnaA RNA-synthesis probability down to v = 0.8e-3 holds the DnaA monomer pool oscillating band-stable within [300,800] across the steady generations with a clean oriC cycle, at the cost of a sub-physiological mRNA initiation rate — establishing a genuine tension between the in-band pool and the ~1/min rate target at this initial condition.

(cistron 227 events/min, [min, mean, max]):

  - ~1/min rate, closest to band: V=1.0e-3 (her guess) — rate dead-on (1.01)

EQUILIBRATION TEST at the now-withdrawn candidate V=1.1e-3 (completed
15-generation run
out/dnaa1_v1p1e-3_long, Mechanism A, seed 1, resumed from the dnaa-0 gen-3
dill; --perturbation 'TU00259[c]=1.1e-3'). The original 7-gen V=1.1e-3 run
showed the DnaA monomer cycle-mean still RAMPING (gens 4-7: 484/573/804/842)
with gens 6-7 just over 800, leaving it ambiguous whether the pool
EQUILIBRATES in [300,800] or keeps drifting over. The 15-gen run settles it.
Per-gen DnaA monomer cycle-mean (canonical all-zeros lineage, bulk
PD03831[c]+MONOMER0-160[c]+MONOMER0-4565[c]):

past 800 to a peak of 976 at gen 9 (and 970 at gen 11; within-cycle peaks

The cell cycle stays healthy throughout (every generation divides, oriC 1↔2, no reinitiation), and the FBA GLP_NOFEAS infeasibilities peak at gen 9 with the DnaA overshoot and vanish by gens 11-15.

studies.name: dnaa-2-nucleotide-balance
studies.title: Study 2 — Validate ATP/ADP Balance
studies.question:
Starting from a V-tuned succinate lineage (total DnaA in [300, 800], clean
cell cycle), how does the DnaA pool partition across forms (apo-DnaA /
DnaA-ATP / DnaA-ADP) once DnaA nucleotide-binding + DnaA-ATP intrinsic
hydrolysis are modelled correctly? Does the DnaA-ATP fraction land in the
biological [0.2, 0.5] band — and if the naive equilibrium pins it near 1.0,
what is the right fix?

resolved_uncertainties: Haochen's bf8b82e mechanism — DnaA + ADP ⇌ DnaA-ADP kept bidirectional but flagged integrate_dt (kinetic, literal k_r = 1×10⁻⁷/s) plus one-way DnaA-ATP intrinsic hydrolysis (k = 0.046/min) — drives the DnaA-ATP fraction off the ~0.997 fast-equilibrium pin into the Boesen [0.2,0.5] band with no rate override.
The ~0.997 pin was a fast-equilibrium modelling artefact (the tick-wise solve reverting kinetically-trapped DnaA-ADP), not a K_d / [ATP]:[ADP] / expected-fraction parameter inconsistency.

Re-verified multi-seed (seeds 0/1/2) on the corrected emitter — all four must-preserve behaviours pass on Rashmi's generation-average criterion (DnaA-ATP fraction avg 0.268/0.267/0.302, total DnaA gen-avg 392/575/578, periodic mass doubling, one oriC initiation per generation). [The original seed-1 0.26/535 reading was on pre-fix truncated data — superseded.]
remaining_uncertainties: The per-generation average DnaA-ATP fraction trends to the low edge of the band in later gens (~0.16–0.23, dipping below 0.2 in gens 5 & 8); where in the band it sits is a k_r-tuning question left for Haochen.

The strict per-generation in-band reproduction is not perfectly clean even on the directed seed (gen-1 burned-in transient above band; later-gen dips below) — a clean strict per-gen 7-gen run with raw data on this branch is still absent (gate_status pending).

alternate_hypotheses.statement: The DnaA-ATP fraction's drift to the low edge of the band in later generations is driven by total DnaA abundance (fraction anti-correlated with total DnaA, r=−0.88), not by any [ATP]:[ADP] nucleotide-ratio drift.
alternate_hypotheses.why_plausible: The background [ATP]:[ADP] ratio is constant at 20.3 across all 8 gens (pinned by metabolism), while the fraction falls from 0.53 to ~0.16–0.23 as the pool grows from ~185 to ~640 — so at the proper [300,800] abundance the kinetic steady state lands at the band's low edge.
evidence_for: r=−0.88 anti-correlation of %DnaA-ATP with total DnaA
k_r sweep lifts the fraction (1e-7→0.314, 1e-5→0.382 at gen-2)
evidence_against: only a single seed (seed 1) was evaluated on this branch's post-#117 code

findings.summary:
DIAGNOSIS (2026-06-04, seed-1 8-gen) of why the DnaA-ATP fraction drifts low
in later generations. The background [ATP]:[ADP] ratio is CONSTANT at 20.3
across all 8 gens (pinned by metabolism) — so the drift is NOT a nucleotide-
ratio drift. Instead the DnaA-ATP fraction is strongly ANTI-correlated with
TOTAL DnaA (r = −0.88): as the pool grows from ~185 (gen-1 transient) to ~640
(later gens, in the [300,800] band), the fraction falls from 0.53 to ~0.16-0.23.
So at the PROPER DnaA abundance (the [300,800] target dnaa-1 tuning achieves),
the kinetic steady state (hydrolysis k=0.046/min draining DnaA-ATP vs slow
ADP-dissociation k_r=1e-7/s re-charging) lands the fraction at the LOW EDGE of
Boesen [0.2,0.5], dipping below 0.2 in some gens. Implication: lifting it
cleanly into the band is a RATE-CONSTANT question (e.g. a modestly faster k_r
→ more re-charging → higher %ATP) — Haochen's lever — NOT a [ATP]:[ADP] or
DnaA-abundance issue. Confirmed by a k_r sweep (1e-7→0.314, 1e-6→0.314,
1e-5→0.382 at gen-2): faster k_r lifts the fraction, ~100× needed.

findings.statement: Ran s=0.7 Hill 3-seed; band-centered for 2/3 seeds; resume-stability probe blocked by a dill-roundtrip tooling bug (documented).
Answered via the homeostasis finding: V is cancelled by feedback; band-centering achieved via s=0.7 (feedback strength is the lever).

Tests run (evaluator): cell-cycle-preserved PASS (robust, all 3 seeds, oriC<=2/0 re-init); DnaA-pool-in-band PARTIAL (strict per-gen FAIL on the g17 partial gen + seed0 noise; 2/3 seeds in-band for full gens g3-16). Not a clean pass -> the box-binding redo on the autoreg expression is pending your call given PARTIAL (and dnaa-4 already runs box-binding UNDER the autoreg expression, so those dynamics are already in the s=0.7 runs).

Box-binding dynamics UNDER the s=0.7 autoregulated expression (analyzed from the existing dnaa4_s07_seed{0,1,2} runs, steady gens >=3): high-affinity boxes stay well-occupied (chromosomal_high 0.70/0.89/0.95, oriC_high 0.69/0.88/0.93, dnaA-promoter_high 0.67/0.86/0.90 across seed0/1/2), while the LOW-AFFINITY oriC boxes (K_d 100 nM) stay MOSTLY EMPTY (0.10/0.15/0.28). The oriC-low over-binding flagged in dnaa-3 (read-only observer ~0.8, active-mechanism adopted ~0.46) is FURTHER RESOLVED under autoregulation — feedback lowers DnaA, depleting the free DnaA-ATP that drove low-affinity over-occupancy, so the low-aff sites fill only transiently. Bound pools are predominantly DnaA-ADP (~20-32% ATP at the high-aff boxes) from intrinsic hydrolysis. Chart: dnaa4_box_dynamics. (Rashmi 2026-06-14: box-binding dynamics on top of the achieved expression dynamics — answered via the existing autoreg runs rather than a fresh study, since dnaa-4 already runs box-binding under autoreg.)

DnaA-ATP-vs-DnaA-ADP noise asymmetry (Haochen 2026-06-14): the DnaA-ADP curve is much SMOOTHER than DnaA-ATP even though ADP is downstream of ATP (ATP hydrolyses to ADP), so ADP should inherit ATP's noise. MECHANISM (where the asymmetry comes from): in flat_overrides/equilibrium_reaction_rates.tsv, DnaA-ATP formation (MONOMER0-160_RXN, apo+ATP<->DnaA-ATP) has integrate_dt=false (FAST-EQUILIBRIUM — re-solved to steady state every tick, so it instantly tracks the stochastic free-ATP/apo pools => noisy), while DnaA-ADP formation (MONOMER0-4565_RXN) and the hydrolysis (DNAA-INTRINSIC-HYDROLYSIS-RXN) are integrate_dt=true (KINETIC ODE integration over dt, which averages out the sub-tick stochasticity => smooth). IMPORTANT — this is NOT a bug: the fast-equilibrium treatment of DnaA+ATP<->DnaA-ATP is a DELIBERATE, physically-justified modeling choice (Haochen: cellular ATP is abundant, so DnaA-ATP binding equilibrates fast — fast-equilibrium is the appropriate approximation) and is the ORIGINAL whole-cell-model treatment. So the smoothness asymmetry is an EXPECTED consequence of that justified design, not an artifact to "correct". EXPERIMENT (Haochen/Eran endorsed "try this too") — RUN AND RESOLVED 2026-06-14: set MONOMER0-160_RXN integrate_dt false->true (kinetic integration of DnaA-ATP formation) to TEST whether the DnaA-ATP curve becomes smoother. Method: rather than a full-ParCa rebuild (which independently fails at the unrelated promoter-binding cvxpy solver, promoter_fitting.py:548 — NOT caused by this flag), the integrate_dt_mask was patched directly in a copy of the canonical cache (cache_dnaa4_autoreg, which already had ADP+hydrolysis kinetic), flipping ONLY MONOMER0-160 to kinetic, then resumed from the seed-1 gen5 dill for gen 6 (s=0.7 Hill, V=1.5e-3, k_h=0.025; gen completed cleanly, tau=59 min, divided). RESULT — NEGATIVE: kinetic ATP did NOT smooth the DnaA-ATP curve. Tick-jitter/mean of the DnaA-ATP form went 0.0082 (fast-eq) -> 0.0132 (kinetic, marginally WORSE), the ATP/ADP asymmetry ratio went 2.11 -> 2.41 (worse), and the ATP fraction shifted 0.327 -> 0.293. CONCLUSION: the asymmetry is NOT a solver-method artifact for ATP — it is a pool-size/topology effect. DnaA-ADP is the larger terminal sink (~278 vs ~132 molecules) that accumulates downstream, so its relative noise is intrinsically lower (~1/sqrt N buffering); DnaA-ATP is the smaller dynamic intermediate (formed by ATP binding, drained by hydrolysis + oriC/box turnover) and necessarily carries the turnover fluctuations. Noise DOES propagate ATP->ADP but is averaged out by the large ADP pool. DECISION (taken): REVERTED MONOMER0-160_RXN integrate_dt back to false — the justified, abundant-ATP, original-WCM fast-equilibrium default stands; the kinetic variant is not adopted (it doesn't help and is marginally worse). Comparison figure: out/dnaa4_atp_kinetic_vs_fasteq_gen6.png. (Residual box-binding free<->bound stochasticity in dnaa_box_binding.py is a separate, smaller noise source; reducing the visible ATP jitter further would mean enlarging/buffering the ATP pool or smoothing the box-binding turnover, NOT changing the equilibrium solver method.)

Band-centering CLOSED via feedback strength (s/seed sweep, 2026-06-15): the dnaa-4 DnaA-pool-in-band test was PARTIAL at s=0.7 — seed 0's per-generation MEAN dipped out of [300,800] at g11-13 (246/187/269) while seeds 1,2 held. A focused sweep (RIDA/DDAH/DARS DISABLED — pure dnaa-4) resuming seed 0 from its gen-8 dill through the failing window g9-14 shows s=0.65 THREADS THE NEEDLE: every generation mean lands in band (409-545) AND the peak stays under 800 (781), converting the previously-failing gens to a clean per-gen PASS. s=0.60 also lifts the means in-band but the peak breaks 800 (827) — too weak. So s=0.65 (Hill K=0.5, n=4, V=1.5e-3, k_h=0.025) is the band-centering value: between s=0.7 (trough dips out) and s=0.6 (peak breaks band). HONEST caveats: (1) the test scores the generation-AVERAGE (operator generation_average_in_range) — at s=0.65 all gen-means are in-band, though the instantaneous trough still grazes ~251 momentarily; (2) this is seed 0 resumed through its dip window — a fully robust clean-pass claim is being confirmed by a 3-seed fresh 16-gen run at s=0.65 (launched 2026-06-15, RIDA/DARS off). DECISION: adopt s=0.65 as canonical (supersedes s=0.7), pending the 3-seed 16-gen confirmation. Runs: dnaa4_band_s065 / dnaa4_band_s060 (sweep); dnaa4_s065_seed{0,1,2}_16gen (confirmation).
